pages.text: Mass is the reactor's fuel. $(thing)Every block counts as 1 mass$(), whatever it is. Materials from the $(l:event_horizon/materials)Event Horizon$() count for far more.$(br2)Insert blocks by hand, with hoppers, or with pipes.$(br2)Once it's running, you can also throw things into the ring: the black hole pulls in anything inside the ring's hole. It pulls on everything in a $(thing)sphere of influence$() that just fits inside the ring, the ground below included: blocks are torn loose a surface at a time, eating a bowl under the core. $(danger)In a failure the sphere grows$(): past the ring in a stall or fault, further in pre-meltdown and after a breach, and much further in a meltdown. Every item and every block is $(num)1$() mass, and a creature is $(num)1$() mass per heart. The mass is split evenly across the four stabilizers.$(br2)The more mass the reactor holds, the $(thing)bigger the black hole$() and the harder it pulls: four times the ignition minimum makes it twice as wide and pull twice as hard.

Each stabilizer needs at least $(num)10,000$() mass before ignition. There is $(thing)no maximum$().$(br2)More mass runs longer, but makes a bigger crater if it all goes wrong.$(br2)A comparator shows how close a port is to the ignition minimum.
pages.title: How much?
Moving structures
pages.text: With $(thing)Sable$() installed (Create: Aeronautics and the like), moving structures aren't safe either. Any that drift into the black hole's reach are reeled in, harder the closer they get, and torn apart a block at a time, nearest first, just like the ground.$(br2)They're worth the same as the ground: see Storage.

pages.title: Storage
pages.text: Chests, barrels, furnaces and anything else that stores items go in too, contents and all: $(num)1$() mass for the block plus $(num)1$() per item inside. A full chest is worth $(num)1,729$().$(br2)This mod's own machines (the laser, consoles, research core, the bomb) are never torn off.$(br2)If a vent lets a torn block fall instead, it lands with its contents back in it.
